questions.prompt: Which farming activity can directly cause soil pollution when done carelessly?
options: Using too much artificial fertilizer
Mulching a vegetable bed
Planting an agroforestry tree
Watering seedlings early in the morning
questions.correctAnswer: Using too much artificial fertilizer
questions.explanation: Excess fertilizer can leave harmful chemicals in the soil and affect soil organisms and crops.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain causes of soil pollution in farming.

questions.prompt: Used chemical containers should be left in the garden for learners to reuse as water cups.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Used chemical containers may contain poison residues and should be disposed of safely according to instructions.
questions.learningOutcome: Promote safe farming practices to prevent soil pollution.

questions.prompt: Which practice best controls soil pollution when applying farm chemicals?
options: Using the recommended type and amount
Mixing many chemicals without reading labels
Pouring leftover chemicals into the soil
Spraying more chemical than the crop needs
questions.correctAnswer: Using the recommended type and amount
questions.explanation: Following recommended rates reduces chemical buildup and keeps the soil safer for crops and organisms.
questions.learningOutcome: Control soil pollution through safe agricultural practices.

questions.prompt: Why are plastic wastes a problem when dumped in cultivated soil?
options: They do not rot easily and can block air and water movement
They immediately turn into compost manure
They make all crop roots stronger
They increase rainfall on the farm
questions.correctAnswer: They do not rot easily and can block air and water movement
questions.explanation: Plastic wastes stay in soil for a long time and can interfere with root growth, water infiltration, and soil life.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how farm wastes can pollute soil.

questions.prompt: Name two farm wastes that can pollute soil if they are dumped carelessly.
questions.correctAnswer: Used chemical containers and plastic waste
questions.explanation: Chemical containers may hold toxic residues, while plastic waste does not decompose easily in soil.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify agricultural wastes that can pollute soil.

questions.prompt: A vegetable crop wilts near a spot where leftover herbicide was poured. What is the most likely cause?
options: Chemical pollution of the soil
Too much agroforestry
Correct mulching practice
Healthy soil organisms
questions.correctAnswer: Chemical pollution of the soil
questions.explanation: Herbicides can harm crops when poured into soil instead of being handled safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze signs of soil pollution caused by unsafe farming practices.

questions.prompt: After using a pesticide container, which action is safest for soil conservation?
options: Dispose of it safely as directed and never reuse it for food or water
Cut it open and use it as a lunch box
Throw it into a nearby crop field
Burn it beside dry grass without adult guidance
questions.correctAnswer: Dispose of it safely as directed and never reuse it for food or water
questions.explanation: Safe disposal prevents chemical residues from entering the soil and protects people and animals.
questions.learningOutcome: Promote responsible disposal of used farm chemical containers.

questions.prompt: Well-prepared compost manure used correctly is less likely to pollute soil than careless dumping of chemicals.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Compost is organic matter, while careless chemical dumping can leave harmful residues in the soil.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare safe and unsafe soil management practices.

questions.prompt: Write one short awareness message that can discourage soil pollution on a school farm.
questions.correctAnswer: Dispose of farm chemical containers and plastic waste safely to keep our soil healthy.
questions.explanation: A good awareness message should name the unsafe practice and encourage a clear action that protects soil.
questions.learningOutcome: Create awareness messages that promote safe farming practices.

questions.prompt: Why is water conservation important in farming?
options: It keeps water available for crops for longer after rains
It makes all weeds disappear permanently
It stops crops from needing sunlight
It changes sandy soil into metal
questions.correctAnswer: It keeps water available for crops for longer after rains
questions.explanation: Conserving water helps crops survive dry periods and supports better growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the importance of water conservation in farming.

questions.prompt: Which structure can collect surface runoff for use by crops?
options: Water retention ditch
Open rubbish heap
Chemical store
Bare footpath
questions.correctAnswer: Water retention ditch
questions.explanation: A water retention ditch slows runoff and allows water to collect or soak into the soil.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify structures used to conserve surface runoff.

questions.prompt: Minimum tillage can conserve soil moisture by reducing unnecessary disturbance of the soil.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Less disturbance helps reduce evaporation and protects soil structure.
questions.learningOutcome: Use minimum tillage practices to conserve water in farming.

questions.prompt: Which practice is an example of minimum tillage for conserving soil moisture?
options: Slashing weeds and leaving mulch on the soil
Digging the whole field deeply every day
Removing all plant cover from the soil
Burning crop residues before every rain
questions.correctAnswer: Slashing weeds and leaving mulch on the soil
questions.explanation: Slashing and mulching disturb the soil less and reduce water loss from the surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify minimum tillage practices that conserve water.

questions.prompt: Where should a water retention ditch usually be placed on a sloping school farm?
options: Across the slope to slow runoff
Straight down the slope to speed runoff
Inside the chemical store
On top of harvested vegetables
questions.correctAnswer: Across the slope to slow runoff
questions.explanation: Placing a ditch across the slope reduces water speed and helps the soil absorb more water.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct water retention structures to conserve surface runoff.

questions.prompt: A learner makes an earth basin around a banana seedling. What is the main purpose?
options: To hold water near the plant
To make the seedling grow without soil
To keep all insects away forever
To stop the plant from using nutrients
questions.correctAnswer: To hold water near the plant
questions.explanation: An earth basin catches water around a plant so it can soak into the root zone.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how earth basins support water conservation.

questions.prompt: State two water retention structures that can conserve surface runoff.
questions.correctAnswer: Water retention ditches and earth basins
questions.explanation: Water retention ditches, earth basins, and retention pits can slow or hold runoff for crop use.
questions.learningOutcome: Name structures used for conserving surface runoff.

questions.prompt: How does restricted cultivation help conserve water in the soil?
options: It leaves more soil undisturbed and reduces evaporation
It removes every root from the soil
It makes runoff move faster
It prevents crops from germinating
questions.correctAnswer: It leaves more soil undisturbed and reduces evaporation
questions.explanation: Disturbing only the needed parts of the field helps the soil keep more moisture.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how minimum tillage practices conserve soil moisture.

questions.prompt: Rainwater is washing soil from a school seedbed. Which action best solves the problem?
options: Make shallow retention pits or ditches to slow the runoff
Remove all crop cover from the seedbed
Pour used pesticide into the water path
Plant seedlings without watering them
questions.correctAnswer: Make shallow retention pits or ditches to slow the runoff
questions.explanation: Retention structures slow water, reduce erosion, and allow more water to soak into the soil.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply water conservation measures to solve runoff problems.

questions.prompt: Deeply digging the whole garden every week is always the best way to conserve soil water.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Frequent deep digging can expose moist soil and increase water loss, while minimum tillage conserves moisture.
questions.learningOutcome: Appraise minimum tillage as a water conservation practice.

questions.prompt: Which water conservation plan is safest near a busy classroom path?
options: Use mulch and a shallow, well-marked basin around the crop
Dig a deep unmarked pit in the path
Leave slippery mud across the doorway
Store dirty water in open drinking bottles
questions.correctAnswer: Use mulch and a shallow, well-marked basin around the crop
questions.explanation: Water conservation should protect crops while also keeping learners safe from falls and contamination.
questions.learningOutcome: Appraise safe water conservation measures in the school environment.

questions.prompt: Which observation shows that a water retention structure is working well?
options: Less runoff damage and moist soil near crops after rain
More gullies forming below the garden
Water flowing faster down the slope
Crops drying faster than before
questions.correctAnswer: Less runoff damage and moist soil near crops after rain
questions.explanation: A good water retention structure slows runoff and improves soil moisture near crops.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate the effectiveness of water conservation structures.

questions.prompt: What is agroforestry?
options: Growing useful trees together with crops or pasture
Keeping animals without any plants
Burning all trees before planting crops
Growing crops only inside a store
questions.correctAnswer: Growing useful trees together with crops or pasture
questions.explanation: Agroforestry combines trees with crops or pasture to support production and environmental conservation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of agroforestry in conserving the environment.

questions.prompt: Every tree species is automatically suitable for planting inside a crop field.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: A good agroforestry tree should fit the farm, grow well with crops, and not cause serious competition.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose appropriate agroforestry trees for conserving the environment.

questions.prompt: Which characteristic makes a tree suitable for agroforestry?
options: It can grow alongside crops and has useful products
It kills every crop planted near it
It must be watered every hour throughout the day
It has no value to people, soil, or animals
questions.correctAnswer: It can grow alongside crops and has useful products
questions.explanation: Suitable agroforestry trees should support the farm by conserving soil, providing products, or improving the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Examine characteristics of agroforestry trees.

questions.prompt: Which benefit can agroforestry provide in a school garden?
options: Reducing soil erosion and providing useful materials
Making all crops grow without water
Removing the need for any crop management
Changing weeds into metal tools
questions.correctAnswer: Reducing soil erosion and providing useful materials
questions.explanation: Agroforestry trees can protect soil, provide shade, offer fodder or fuelwood, and improve the farm environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the importance of agroforestry in conserving the environment.

questions.prompt: Which tree choice is best for a crop field where learners want both conservation and crop growth?
options: A fast-growing multipurpose tree that does not heavily shade crops
A tree known to poison nearby crops
A tree planted so densely that no crop receives light
A tree chosen only because it has thorns
questions.correctAnswer: A fast-growing multipurpose tree that does not heavily shade crops
questions.explanation: Agroforestry trees should conserve the environment while allowing crops to grow successfully.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose appropriate agroforestry trees for conserving the environment.

questions.prompt: Give one environmental benefit of planting agroforestry trees on a farm.
questions.correctAnswer: They reduce soil erosion
questions.explanation: Agroforestry trees can hold soil, reduce wind and water erosion, and improve the farm environment.
questions.learningOutcome: State benefits of agroforestry in conserving the environment.

questions.prompt: Learners want to plant a tree along a school fence for agroforestry. Which factor should they consider first?
options: Whether the tree can grow well in the local environment without harming nearby crops
Whether the tree makes the fence impossible to access
Whether the tree blocks all sunlight from the garden
Whether the tree requires polluted water only
questions.correctAnswer: Whether the tree can grow well in the local environment without harming nearby crops
questions.explanation: A suitable agroforestry tree should match the local environment and support the farm system.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate agroforestry trees for a school environment.

questions.prompt: What should learners do soon after planting an agroforestry seedling?
options: Water it and protect it from damage
Pull it out to check the roots every day
Leave it uncovered in a busy path
Pour used chemical near its stem
questions.correctAnswer: Water it and protect it from damage
questions.explanation: Young tree seedlings need water, protection, and regular care until they are well established.
questions.learningOutcome: Establish agroforestry trees for conservation of the environment.

questions.prompt: Agroforestry can conserve the environment while also providing useful products to people or animals.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Agroforestry may provide products such as fodder, fruits, shade, fuelwood, and soil protection.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the importance of agroforestry in conserving the environment.

questions.prompt: A crop near an agroforestry tree is weak because the tree shade is too heavy. What is the best response?
options: Prune the tree responsibly or improve spacing after seeking guidance
Pour chemicals on the tree roots
Remove all trees from the school compound forever
Stop watering the crop completely
questions.correctAnswer: Prune the tree responsibly or improve spacing after seeking guidance
questions.explanation: Good agroforestry management balances tree benefits with crop needs for light, water, and space.
questions.learningOutcome: Appraise management of agroforestry trees in crop fields.

questions.prompt: Which site is most suitable for preparing a school vegetable planting bed?
options: A well-drained place with enough sunlight
A dark corner flooded with wastewater
A path where learners walk every minute
A store room with no soil or light
questions.correctAnswer: A well-drained place with enough sunlight
questions.explanation: Most vegetables need adequate light and a site where excess water can drain away.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify suitable planting sites for crops in the school environment.

questions.prompt: Which tilth is most suitable for very small seeds in a seedbed?
options: Fine tilth
Large unbroken clods
Stony compacted soil
Dry plastic waste
questions.correctAnswer: Fine tilth
questions.explanation: Small seeds need fine soil particles for close contact with moisture and easier germination.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare planting sites according to the planting material.

questions.prompt: Which planting material usually needs a coarser tilth than tiny seeds?
options: A cassava cutting or tuber
A tiny carrot seed
A small amaranth seed
A dust-sized seed sample
questions.correctAnswer: A cassava cutting or tuber
questions.explanation: Large planting materials such as cuttings and tubers can be established in a coarser tilth than tiny seeds.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate planting site preparation to planting material.

questions.prompt: Containers can be used as planting sites when ground space is limited.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Container gardening allows crops to be grown where land is limited, including school compounds and small spaces.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify different planting sites in the school environment.

questions.prompt: Which safety practice should learners follow when preparing a planting site with hoes?
options: Work with enough spacing between learners
Swing tools close to another learner's legs
Run while carrying a raised hoe
Leave sharp tools hidden in grass
questions.correctAnswer: Work with enough spacing between learners
questions.explanation: Safe spacing reduces accidents when learners use tools during site preparation.
questions.learningOutcome: Show responsibility while preparing planting sites.

questions.prompt: A planting site is close to a footpath and seedlings are often stepped on. What should learners do?
options: Choose a protected site or fence the bed clearly
Plant more seedlings directly on the path
Stop all crop production in the school
Pour water on the path to make it slippery
questions.correctAnswer: Choose a protected site or fence the bed clearly
questions.explanation: A planting site should protect crops from trampling while keeping the school environment safe.
questions.learningOutcome: Examine planting sites in relation to crop safety and establishment.

questions.prompt: Give two examples of planting sites that can be used in a school environment.
questions.correctAnswer: Ground seedbed and container site
questions.explanation: Schools can use ground beds, containers, wall spaces, fences, or other suitable areas for planting crops.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify planting sites for crops in the school environment.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is suitable when preparing a simple ground seedbed?
options: Clear weeds, loosen soil, break clods, and level the bed
Harvest crops, pack honey, then throw plastic on the bed
Water the path, remove all tools, and leave stones in place
Plant first, then choose the site after germination
questions.correctAnswer: Clear weeds, loosen soil, break clods, and level the bed
questions.explanation: A seedbed is prepared by clearing, loosening, breaking clods, and leveling to support germination.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare a suitable site for establishing selected planting material.

questions.prompt: Which pair shows the two broad categories of crop planting materials?
options: Seeds and vegetative materials
Honey and eggs
Pets and draught animals
Plastics and chemical containers
questions.correctAnswer: Seeds and vegetative materials
questions.explanation: Crops can be established using seeds or vegetative materials such as cuttings, tubers, and suckers.
questions.learningOutcome: Categorize planting materials used for establishing various crops.

questions.prompt: Which seed sample should be rejected for planting?
options: Wrinkled and damaged seeds
Mature clean seeds
Healthy seeds of the recommended variety
Seeds stored safely in a dry container
questions.correctAnswer: Wrinkled and damaged seeds
questions.explanation: Damaged or wrinkled seeds may have poor viability and can lead to poor germination.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable planting materials for crop establishment.

questions.prompt: Which cutting is most suitable for establishing a crop by vegetative propagation?
options: A healthy mature cutting from a suitable parent plant
A dry rotten cutting with no buds
A very young weak cutting that breaks easily
A cutting soaked in used pesticide
questions.correctAnswer: A healthy mature cutting from a suitable parent plant
questions.explanation: Healthy mature vegetative materials are more likely to establish well after planting.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable vegetative materials for crop establishment.

questions.prompt: Which planting method spreads small seeds over a seedbed or field surface?
options: Broadcasting
Earthing up
Castration
Honey straining
questions.correctAnswer: Broadcasting
questions.explanation: Broadcasting means scattering seeds over a prepared area.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe methods of planting crop materials.

questions.prompt: Which planting method places seeds in continuous shallow rows?
options: Drilling
Random dumping
Grading
Overloading
questions.correctAnswer: Drilling
questions.explanation: Drilling places seeds in rows, making spacing and management easier.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe methods of planting crop materials on a seedbed.

questions.prompt: Which planting method places individual seeds in separate holes?
options: Dibbling
Slashing
Straining
Pruning
questions.correctAnswer: Dibbling
questions.explanation: Dibbling involves making holes and placing seeds in them at suitable spacing.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe methods of planting crop materials.

questions.prompt: Weather information can help learners predict a suitable time for planting rain-fed crops.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Weather forecasts and rainfall information help farmers plan planting when soil moisture is likely to be enough.
questions.learningOutcome: Predict appropriate time of planting using digital information centres.

questions.prompt: Which factor should learners consider before planting a crop that depends on rain?
options: Onset of rain and soil moisture
Colour of the classroom wall only
Number of desks in the room
Whether eggs have been graded
questions.correctAnswer: Onset of rain and soil moisture
questions.explanation: Rain-fed crops establish better when soil moisture is enough at planting time.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine appropriate time of planting different propagation materials.

questions.prompt: Why might a farmer plant the same vegetable crop in small batches at different times?
options: To get a more continuous harvest
To make all seedlings die together
To avoid all crop management practices
To stop the crop from needing soil
questions.correctAnswer: To get a more continuous harvest
questions.explanation: Staggered planting spreads harvest periods and can help meet market or household needs over time.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine planting time based on harvest and market needs.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to handle chemically treated seeds during planting?
options: Use protective care and avoid eating or touching the mouth
Taste the seeds to check quality
Share the seeds as snacks
Wash the colour off in a stream
questions.correctAnswer: Use protective care and avoid eating or touching the mouth
questions.explanation: Treated seeds may contain chemicals, so learners should handle them carefully under guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Select and handle planting materials safely.

questions.prompt: Which option contains only vegetative planting materials?
options: Cassava cutting and banana sucker
Maize seed and bean seed
Honey and egg
Plastic bottle and fertilizer bag
questions.correctAnswer: Cassava cutting and banana sucker
questions.explanation: Cuttings and suckers are vegetative materials used to establish new plants without seeds.
questions.learningOutcome: Categorize planting materials as seeds or vegetative materials.

questions.prompt: A learner plants tiny seeds too deep and they fail to emerge. What mistake was most likely made?
options: The planting depth was too deep for the seed size
The learner used a clean seedbed
The seedbed had enough moisture
The learner labelled the crop correctly
questions.correctAnswer: The planting depth was too deep for the seed size
questions.explanation: Small seeds may not have enough stored food to push through deep soil, so they need shallow planting.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze establishment problems caused by unsuitable planting methods.

questions.prompt: What is a weed in a cultivated field?
options: A plant growing where it is not wanted
Any crop planted in rows
A harvested animal product
A clean planting container
questions.correctAnswer: A plant growing where it is not wanted
questions.explanation: A weed competes with the desired crop for resources such as water, nutrients, light, and space.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate between a weed and a crop in a cultivated field.

questions.prompt: Which method is a physical way of controlling weeds?
options: Uprooting weeds by hand
Ignoring weeds until harvest
Pouring honey on the field
Overloading animals
questions.correctAnswer: Uprooting weeds by hand
questions.explanation: Physical weed control includes uprooting, slashing, and tilling weeds.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out weeding using physical methods.

questions.prompt: Thinning removes extra seedlings so that the remaining plants have enough space.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Thinning reduces overcrowding and helps remaining plants use water, nutrients, and light better.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out thinning for optimum plant spacing.

questions.prompt: What is gapping in crop management?
options: Filling spaces where seeds failed to germinate
Removing all crops before they grow
Grading eggs by size
Keeping pets in dirty housing
questions.correctAnswer: Filling spaces where seeds failed to germinate
questions.explanation: Gapping replaces missing plants so the field has a better plant population.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out gapping for optimum plant spacing.

questions.prompt: What does earthing up mean in crop production?
options: Heaping soil around the base of a growing crop
Removing all soil from crop roots
Packing honey in glass jars
Sorting eggs by shell colour
questions.correctAnswer: Heaping soil around the base of a growing crop
questions.explanation: Earthing up supports the plant, protects roots, and can help tubers develop well.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out earthing up for a suitable crop.

questions.prompt: Which crop would most likely benefit from earthing up around its base?
options: Irish potato
A harvested egg
Packed honey
A pet cat
questions.correctAnswer: Irish potato
questions.explanation: Earthing up is useful for tuber crops such as potatoes because it supports tuber development and protects them.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply earthing up to a suitable crop.

questions.prompt: What is hardening of seedlings?
options: Gradually exposing seedlings to field conditions before transplanting
Drying seedlings until they die
Covering seedlings in plastic waste
Feeding seedlings to pets
questions.correctAnswer: Gradually exposing seedlings to field conditions before transplanting
questions.explanation: Hardening prepares seedlings for conditions outside the nursery and reduces transplanting shock.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out hardening on a suitable crop.

questions.prompt: Why should weeds be controlled in a young vegetable crop?
options: They compete with crops for water, nutrients, light, and space
They automatically become marketable vegetables
They make all crop pests disappear
They reduce the need for seed selection
questions.correctAnswer: They compete with crops for water, nutrients, light, and space
questions.explanation: Weeds reduce crop growth by using resources that the crop needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of crop management practices.

questions.prompt: A seedbed has many overcrowded seedlings. Which management practice should be done first?
options: Thinning
Honey processing
Pet vaccination
Egg grading
questions.correctAnswer: Thinning
questions.explanation: Thinning removes excess seedlings so that the remaining ones grow with proper spacing.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply thinning to improve plant spacing.

questions.prompt: Name two crop management practices taught in Grade 7 Agriculture.
questions.correctAnswer: Weeding and earthing up
questions.explanation: Crop management practices include weeding, thinning, gapping, earthing up, and hardening.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall crop management practices used in crop production.

questions.prompt: Which action shows humane handling of an animal?
options: Guiding it calmly and avoiding injury
Beating it to move faster
Overloading it with heavy goods
Transporting it without air or space
questions.correctAnswer: Guiding it calmly and avoiding injury
questions.explanation: Humane handling protects animal welfare and reduces stress, fear, and injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Handle animals humanely in the community.

questions.prompt: Which example is an inhumane treatment of animals?
options: Overworking a draught animal without rest
Providing clean water to a goat
Using a safe restraint under guidance
Giving an animal enough space during transport
questions.correctAnswer: Overworking a draught animal without rest
questions.explanation: Overworking causes suffering and is a form of mistreatment.
questions.learningOutcome: Examine forms of animal handling in the community.

questions.prompt: Overloading draught animals is a form of animal mistreatment.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Overloading causes pain, tiredness, and possible injury to the animal.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify inhumane treatment of animals in the community.

questions.prompt: Which restraint method is most responsible when handling a docile farm animal?
options: Use an approved method that does not injure the animal
Tie the animal with a wire that cuts the skin
Pull the tail until the animal stops moving
Leave the animal trapped in direct sun all day
questions.correctAnswer: Use an approved method that does not injure the animal
questions.explanation: Safe restraint protects both the handler and the animal from injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe ways of handling animals.

questions.prompt: Which transport practice protects goats during a short journey?
options: Providing enough space, ventilation, and gentle loading
Packing many goats tightly with no air
Throwing goats onto the vehicle quickly
Transporting goats with sharp scrap metal
questions.correctAnswer: Providing enough space, ventilation, and gentle loading
questions.explanation: Animals need safe loading, enough space, and ventilation during transport.
questions.learningOutcome: Defend animals against mistreatment during transport.

questions.prompt: Which statement is best about castration of animals?
options: It should be done using approved methods by a trained person
It should be done by any learner during break time
It should use dirty tools to save time
It should be done without caring about pain or infection
questions.correctAnswer: It should be done using approved methods by a trained person
questions.explanation: Approved methods and skilled handling reduce pain, injury, and infection risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Defend animals against inappropriate handling practices.

questions.prompt: Which message best creates awareness about humane treatment of animals?
options: Handle animals gently and give them water, rest, and safe shelter
Beat animals whenever they move slowly
Keep animals without food to make them quiet
Ignore injured animals until market day
questions.correctAnswer: Handle animals gently and give them water, rest, and safe shelter
questions.explanation: Awareness messages should promote care, safety, and respect for animal welfare.
questions.learningOutcome: Create awareness on the importance of humane treatment of animals.

questions.prompt: A cow refuses to move while being led. What should a humane handler do?
options: Stay calm, check for fear or injury, and guide it gently
Hit it repeatedly with a stick
Twist its tail until it runs
Deny it water for the rest of the day
questions.correctAnswer: Stay calm, check for fear or injury, and guide it gently
questions.explanation: Calm handling reduces stress and helps the handler identify problems such as injury or fear.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safe responses during animal handling.

questions.prompt: Which animal is commonly reared as a pet in many communities?
options: Cat
Termite
Tilapia in a river
Wild hyena
questions.correctAnswer: Cat
questions.explanation: Cats are commonly kept as pets in homes, while wild animals should not be kept casually.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify pets reared in the community.

questions.prompt: Which factor should a family consider before choosing a pet?
options: Safety, cost, space, and legal requirements
Only the pet's colour
How much soil pollution it can cause
Whether it can grade eggs
questions.correctAnswer: Safety, cost, space, and legal requirements
questions.explanation: Responsible pet selection considers welfare, safety, affordability, space, and community rules.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe factors considered in selecting a pet for rearing.

questions.prompt: Local laws, by-laws, and family values should be considered before keeping a pet.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Pet ownership should respect community rules, safety, family agreement, and animal welfare.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe social and legal factors in choosing a pet.

questions.prompt: Which is an ethical way to acquire a pet?
options: Receiving one as a gift from a responsible owner
Stealing a neighbour's puppy
Capturing a protected wild animal
Taking an animal without asking the owner
questions.correctAnswer: Receiving one as a gift from a responsible owner
questions.explanation: Pets should be acquired legally and responsibly through buying, adoption, gifts, or inheritance where appropriate.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how to acquire a pet for rearing.

questions.prompt: Which list contains good management practices for pets?
options: Feeding, housing, sanitation, and disease control
Starving, beating, hiding, and overworking
Broadcasting, drilling, dibbling, and thinning
Crushing, straining, grading, and packing only
questions.correctAnswer: Feeding, housing, sanitation, and disease control
questions.explanation: Pets need food, clean housing, sanitation, parasite control, and disease care.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe management practices in rearing pets.

questions.prompt: What type of housing is best for a pet rabbit?
options: A clean, dry, secure, and well-ventilated shelter
A wet box with sharp nails
An open road with no protection
A dirty chemical container
questions.correctAnswer: A clean, dry, secure, and well-ventilated shelter
questions.explanation: Good housing protects a pet from injury, bad weather, disease, and predators.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply good housing practices in pet management.

questions.prompt: A pet dog is weak and has stopped eating. What should a responsible learner do first?
options: Inform an adult and seek veterinary advice
Ignore it until it recovers alone
Share human medicine without guidance
Tie it in direct sun without water
questions.correctAnswer: Inform an adult and seek veterinary advice
questions.explanation: Sick pets need prompt care from adults and qualified animal health providers.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply disease control and care practices in pet management.

questions.prompt: A family has very little space and a child is allergic to animal fur. What is the best decision about keeping a furry pet?
options: Delay or choose a safer option after considering health and space
Keep many furry pets in one small room
Ignore the allergy because pets do not need planning
Hide the pet from adults and neighbours
questions.correctAnswer: Delay or choose a safer option after considering health and space
questions.explanation: Responsible pet selection considers safety, health, space, cost, and welfare before acquiring the pet.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze factors considered in selecting a pet for rearing.

questions.prompt: Why are eggs sorted and graded?
options: To group them by quality and purpose
To make every egg hatch immediately
To turn them into honey
To stop hens from laying
questions.correctAnswer: To group them by quality and purpose
questions.explanation: Sorting and grading eggs helps identify quality, size, cleanliness, and best use or market category.
questions.learningOutcome: Sort and grade eggs for various purposes.

questions.prompt: Cracked eggs are generally better for long storage than clean uncracked eggs.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Cracked eggs spoil more easily and can allow germs to enter.
questions.learningOutcome: Sort eggs according to quality for safe use and storage.

questions.prompt: Which factor is useful when grading eggs?
options: Size, cleanliness, and shell condition
Colour of the classroom floor
Number of weeds in a seedbed
Depth of a water retention pit only
questions.correctAnswer: Size, cleanliness, and shell condition
questions.explanation: Egg grading looks at features such as size, cleanliness, cracks, and shell quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Sort and grade eggs for various purposes.

questions.prompt: Which method can be used to process raw honey from combs?
options: Crushing and straining
Thinning and gapping
Dibbling and drilling
Overloading and beating
questions.correctAnswer: Crushing and straining
questions.explanation: Raw honey can be removed from combs by crushing the comb and straining out wax and particles.
questions.learningOutcome: Process raw honey from the combs.

questions.prompt: Which container is suitable for packing processed honey?
options: A clean, food-safe glass or plastic container with a lid
A dirty pesticide bottle
A rusty open tin with holes
A used fuel container
questions.correctAnswer: A clean, food-safe glass or plastic container with a lid
questions.explanation: Honey should be packed in clean food-safe containers to prevent contamination and leakage.
questions.learningOutcome: Pack processed honey for storage and use.

questions.prompt: Why should honey never be packed in a used chemical container?
options: Chemical residues can contaminate the honey
It makes the honey more nutritious
It improves the honey colour safely
It helps bees build more combs in the jar
questions.correctAnswer: Chemical residues can contaminate the honey
questions.explanation: Used chemical containers may poison food products and should not be reused for honey.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe packing practices for animal products.

questions.prompt: What is one reason for packing processed honey properly?
options: To keep it clean for storage, use, or marketing
To make it mix with soil
To stop it from being a food product
To turn it into eggs
questions.correctAnswer: To keep it clean for storage, use, or marketing
questions.explanation: Proper packing protects honey quality and makes it easier to store, use, transport, or sell.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of packing processed honey.

questions.prompt: Name two animal products covered under preparation of animal products.
questions.correctAnswer: Eggs and honey
questions.explanation: Grade 7 learners practise sorting and grading eggs and processing and packing honey.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify animal products prepared for use, storage, or marketing.

questions.prompt: Which action shows integrity when preparing honey for sale?
options: Packing clean honey without adding water or foreign materials
Mixing honey with dirty water to increase volume
Hiding wax and soil in the honey
Using a false label to mislead buyers
questions.correctAnswer: Packing clean honey without adding water or foreign materials
questions.explanation: Integrity in preparing animal products means keeping products clean, honest, and safe for users.
questions.learningOutcome: Embrace ethical preparation of animal products for storage and marketing.

questions.prompt: What is off-season cropping?
options: Growing crops outside the usual rainy or main growing season using suitable techniques
Stopping all farming until the next year
Growing crops only after they have been harvested
Keeping pets instead of growing crops
questions.correctAnswer: Growing crops outside the usual rainy or main growing season using suitable techniques
questions.explanation: Off-season cropping uses techniques and technologies that allow crops to grow beyond the normal season.
questions.learningOutcome: Discuss the meaning of off-season cropping as a farming technique.

questions.prompt: Which is an important benefit of off-season vegetable production?
options: Continuous supply of food
Permanent removal of all pests
No need for water at any stage
Automatic soil pollution
questions.correctAnswer: Continuous supply of food
questions.explanation: Off-season cropping can improve food security by making vegetables available beyond the main season.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of off-season cropping in agriculture.

questions.prompt: Which technology can support off-season cropping by using water efficiently?
options: Drip irrigation
Egg grading tray
Animal harness
Honey strainer
questions.correctAnswer: Drip irrigation
questions.explanation: Drip irrigation applies water near plant roots and can reduce wastage during dry periods.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose appropriate technology to support off-season cropping.

questions.prompt: How can container gardening support off-season cropping in a school with limited land?
options: It allows crops to be grown in movable containers using small spaces
It makes crops grow without light or water
It replaces the need for planting materials
It is only used for transporting goats
questions.correctAnswer: It allows crops to be grown in movable containers using small spaces
questions.explanation: Container gardening helps farmers use limited spaces and manage water more closely.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe technologies used in off-season cropping.

questions.prompt: Why might a farmer use timed planting for an off-season crop?
options: To match harvest time with food needs or market demand
To ensure all seeds are planted too deep
To avoid planning water supply
To prevent any crop from being harvested
questions.correctAnswer: To match harvest time with food needs or market demand
questions.explanation: Timed planting helps farmers plan production for a target harvest period.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe techniques used in off-season cropping.

questions.prompt: What is staggered planting?
options: Planting the same crop in intervals rather than all at once
Planting all seeds in one crowded hole
Planting only cracked eggs
Planting without a site
questions.correctAnswer: Planting the same crop in intervals rather than all at once
questions.explanation: Staggered planting spreads production and harvest over a longer period.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe techniques used in off-season cropping.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes succession planting?
options: Planting another crop after one crop is harvested or nearly finished
Planting no crop after harvesting
Keeping animals in a crop field permanently
Mixing honey with water before packing
questions.correctAnswer: Planting another crop after one crop is harvested or nearly finished
questions.explanation: Succession planting keeps land productive by following one crop with another in a planned sequence.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe appropriate techniques used in off-season cropping.

questions.prompt: Off-season cropping can help a farmer earn regular income when produce is scarce.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Off-season produce may provide income because food is available when fewer farmers are harvesting.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of off-season cropping in agriculture.

questions.prompt: Which plan best handles water scarcity in off-season vegetable production?
options: Use drip irrigation, mulch, and careful watering
Leave the soil bare and water randomly
Plant without any water source
Dig channels that drain water away from crops
questions.correctAnswer: Use drip irrigation, mulch, and careful watering
questions.explanation: Efficient watering and mulch reduce water loss and help crops grow during dry periods.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose appropriate technology to support off-season cropping.

questions.prompt: Which crop is generally practical for a small container garden used for off-season learning?
options: Leafy vegetables such as spinach or kales
A full-grown mango orchard in one small tin
A mature eucalyptus forest in one bucket
A sugarcane plantation inside a desk drawer
questions.correctAnswer: Leafy vegetables such as spinach or kales
questions.explanation: Leafy vegetables can grow in containers when soil, water, nutrients, and light are well managed.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose appropriate crops and technologies for off-season container gardening.

questions.prompt: A school wants vegetables during a dry month but has limited water and land. Which plan is most suitable?
options: Grow vegetables in containers using mulch and controlled watering
Broadcast seeds on bare dry ground and leave them
Plant a crop in an unmarked footpath
Store seeds until they rot
questions.correctAnswer: Grow vegetables in containers using mulch and controlled watering
questions.explanation: Container gardening with moisture conservation can support off-season production in limited space.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze appropriate technologies for off-season cropping in limited spaces.

questions.prompt: Name two techniques used in off-season cropping.
questions.correctAnswer: Staggered planting and succession planting
questions.explanation: Off-season cropping can use techniques such as timed planting, staggered planting, and succession planting.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall techniques used in off-season cropping.

questions.prompt: Which low-cost technology would most likely improve water use in a small off-season vegetable plot?
options: A simple drip line from a raised water container
A leaking bucket placed far from the crop
A broken pesticide sprayer used for drinking water
A dry seed tray with no drainage or soil
questions.correctAnswer: A simple drip line from a raised water container
questions.explanation: A simple drip system can deliver water near crop roots and reduce wastage.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate technologies that support off-season cropping.

questions.prompt: Propose a simple off-season vegetable project for a school with limited space and explain why it can work.
questions.correctAnswer: Use containers to grow leafy vegetables, apply mulch, water carefully, and plant in intervals so the school gets a steady supply.
questions.explanation: A strong plan should match the available space, conserve water, use suitable crops, and explain how production will continue.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a practical plan for off-season crop production using appropriate techniques and technologies.
